content.text: {"kind":"note","label":"Project identity in PANopt: path vs repo, and why derivation fails (forks)"}

content.text:
Spun out of the multi-project switcher design ([[#119]]). Concern raised: a
project's identity is currently a filesystem **path**, but a project is really
**repo**-based, and a repo can be cloned into any path. Drives todo #124.

# Today (path-based identity)
- `projects.root TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` = canonicalized absolute path.
- DESIGN.md §5.3 documents this deliberately: "distinct git worktrees are
  distinct projects unless deliberately pointed at the same path." Reads as a
  consequence acknowledged, not a concern resolved.
- `?ws=<path>` does **double duty**: it is both the **identity key** (the DB
  row) AND the **projection location** (where `.panopt/*.md` is written).

# What path-identity breaks
- Same repo cloned to a different path -> different project; state doesn't
  follow.
- `mv`/rename a checkout -> new project, old state orphaned.
- Two worktrees / a throwaway hotfix clone -> the repo's backlog fragments.
- Cross-machine (the remote/multiplayer thread, [[#118]]) -> same codebase has
  a different path on each host, so each daemon sees a separate project.
  Repo-based identity is exactly what lets agents on different hosts/paths
  coordinate as one project.

# The key structural insight
Split the two roles `?ws=` currently conflates:
- **Identity** -> a stable repo key, resolved **at the edge** (launcher /
  `agent-config`), passed as a distinct `project=` parameter. `panopt-core`
  stays an opaque-key store, so no git dependency crosses the core boundary
  (forbidden by the workspace layout anyway).
- **Projection** -> stays per-checkout `ws=<path>`; each working tree mirrors
  the repo's state locally. (Projection is inherently path-bound; identity is
  not.)

# Why you cannot DERIVE identity from git: the fork problem
A fork shares the **entire history**, root commit included, so
`git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD` returns the **identical** root-commit hash
for upstream and every fork (and for a clone that later diverged). Root-commit
hash therefore **over-merges**: it answers "same history?" when the real
question is "same project?", and a fork is exactly where those two questions
diverge. Two trees with identical history may be one project or two - and
**only a human knows which**. Identity is *intent*, not data.

Each derivable key just encodes a different policy:
| key | policy | effect on a fork |
|---|---|---|
| root-commit hash | "same history = same project" | MERGES fork into upstream |
| remote origin URL | "same push target = same project" | SPLITS fork off (often right); fragile - URL changes, local-only repos have none |
| canonical path | "same checkout = same project" | splits everything, even your own two clones |
| committed UUID | "same project = whatever the repo declares" | YOU decide |

(NOTE: this corrects [[#119]], where root-commit hash was wrongly the lead
candidate. Forks kill it.)

# Recommendation: declaration on top of a fallback resolver
Identity = a `.panopt/project-id` (UUID) **committed into the tree** when
present; else a derived fallback. The committed id travels across clones,
moves, machines, and worktrees because it is *in the tree*, and it makes the
fork question explicit:
- A fork inherits upstream's UUID by default (the file rides along in the copy).
- Want the fork to be its own project? `panopt project init` rewrites the UUID
  - one intentional command.
- Two checkouts of your own repo already share the UUID -> unified, no action.
- Collision only matters **within one daemon**, so "inherits by default, opt
  into split" is safe: the only time upstream==fork bites is when both are
  checked out against the same daemon, and that's a one-command fix.

Resolver order (resolved at the edge, passed as opaque `project=`):
1. `.panopt/project-id` committed in the tree -> **authoritative**.
2. else normalized remote origin URL (strip scheme/credentials/`.git`,
   lowercase host).
3. else root-commit hash (local repo, no remote).
4. else canonical path (not a git repo).

# Open questions
- Default for a freshly cloned fork: inherit (current proposal) vs. prompt on
  first `up`. Leaning inherit + easy re-init.
- Migration of existing path-keyed `projects.root` rows to the new scheme
  (forward-only `user_version` step; back-fill a derived key per existing row).
- Where the UUID file lives and whether it is `.gitignore`-able vs.
  meant-to-commit (must be committed to travel - that is the whole point).
- Interaction with the switcher board ([[#119]]): a project row keys on repo
  identity and lists its *checkouts* (paths/sessions) beneath it.

content.text: Todo **#124** already exists as the umbrella ("Redesign project identity…") and it even enumerates work items. So "make todos from it" most likely means breaking #124's work items into discrete, sequenced todos. Let me check existing todos to avoid dupes, read the switcher note #119, and explore the actual code paths.

Design exploration spun out of the #117 / note #118 Zellij research. Question:
how should PANopt handle **multiple projects**? Today we punt and defer to
multiple `panopt` invocations. Follow-up todos: #120 (project_list MCP tool),
#121 (cold-start handoff spike). Related: [[#118]].

# Ground truth: what a "project" actually is today
- **Daemon: already multi-project.** `panopt-core` keys everything on
  `project: i64` - roster, locks, todos, notes all project-isolated
  (registry.rs, locks.rs). One DB, one daemon on 127.0.0.1:7600. The
  `projects` table stores `root TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` - i.e. **the daemon
  persists every project's absolute path**. MCP connections pick their project
  via `?ws=<abs-path>`. A second `panopt up` in another repo **reuses** the
  running daemon (`daemon::ensure` no-ops if the port is open).
- **Cockpit: single-project.** `session_name(project)` =
  `panopt-<basename>-<pathhash>`, and the layout bakes one `PROJECT` into every
  sidebar pane's `ws`/`cwd`. One Zellij session = one project's cockpit.

So "multiple instances" today is really **one shared daemon + N independent
cockpit sessions**, not multiple backends.

# The crux
The UI unit of "a project" is the **sidebar** (the five plugin panes, each
pinned to one `ws`). "Multiple projects in one cockpit" therefore means
**multiple sidebars**, and Zellij's only native container for that is **tabs**.
(Panes don't help: dropping project B's pane into project A's cockpit leaves
the sidebar still showing A.)

# Tabs vs. instances (compare & contrast)
| axis | multiple instances (today) | multiple tabs (tab/project) |
|---|---|---|
| new code | none | substantial |
| switch | detach/attach or OS window | Zellij tab key, in-viewport |
| single pane of glass | no | yes (tab bar = project list) |
| isolation | hard (separate sessions) | soft (shared session) |
| sidebar instances | 5 per open session | 5 x #tabs in one session |
| per-project multiplayer | natural (mirroring is per-session, #116) | broken (see below) |
| lifecycle | quit/resurrect one freely | one session; quit risks all |

Three things the **tab model fights** today:
1. `ws` is baked per-pane; `new_tab_template` is static and can't vary `ws` per
   tab, so native new-tab can't know which project a tab is for - PANopt would
   have to own tab creation.
2. Pipe narrowing is `mode`-only, not `ws`+`mode`; a broadcast `panopt:*` pipe
   would hit every project-tab's todos gatekeeper. The whole gate layer would
   need ws-awareness.
3. `mirror_session true` (#116) shares the active tab across clients, so two
   teammates can't sit on different project-tabs. (Unreleased Zellij changelog
   hints at per-client tab focus - "allow tabs to have different sizes if
   clients aren't focused on the same one" - but not shipped.)

Conclusion: don't cram projects into one session via tabs. **Stay
multi-session for isolation and add a project switcher.** Tabs become a clean
follow-on only once Zellij ships per-client tab focus AND the gate layer is
ws-aware.

# The switcher: why it's cheap
It's a **join of three things PANopt already has**, on a key it computes
deterministically:

    projects.root --session_name()--> expected Zellij session
                  --`zellij list-sessions`--> running? stopped? absent?
        + active_counts_by_project() + todo aggregates --> live badges

- `projects.root` gives the path; `session_name(root)` gives the session name
  (same fn the launcher uses).
- `active_counts_by_project()` already exists and is used in state.rs:216.
- up.rs:417 already shells `zellij list-sessions` and parses it
  (`session_state`, `strip_ansi`).
So the board is largely a *view*; the only net-new runtime mechanic is
cold-start handoff (#121).

# What each project row shows
    ● panopt    2 agents · 4 in-progress · 11 open    ~/cp/panopt
    ○ frontend  idle                                  ~/work/frontend  [stopped]
    ◌ infra     1 agent ⚠ waiting                      ~/ops/infra      [never started]
- glyph: ● live cockpit · ○ stopped/resurrectable · ◌ daemon state, no session.
- badges (all from data the daemon already holds): active agents, in-progress +
  open todos, locks held, last activity.
- `⚠ waiting` (agent idle at a prompt) makes the board a triage board, not just
  a launcher - this is where the #118 scrollback / `zellij subscribe`
  capability pays off.

# Three switching mechanics (target state decides the gesture)
1. **Live cockpit** -> plugin `switch_session(name)` (instant; source cockpit
   keeps running). From outside: `zellij attach <name>`.
2. **Stopped/resurrectable** -> `zellij attach` resurrects, or offer delete
   (up.rs already handles the dead-session case).
3. **Never started** -> bootstrap (generate layout+config, register row, start
   session, attach). This cold-start handoff is the one genuinely new mechanic
   -> #121.

# Form factors (complementary)
- **(A) Home session** - `panopt` with no args attaches a dedicated
  `panopt-home` session whose sole content is the board. Morning entry point /
  fallback. One session, one pane, no per-project sidebar.
- **(B) Floating quick-switch** - a hotkey (e.g. `Alt-0`, next to the
  `Alt-1..5` sidebar-focus binds) floats the same board over the current
  cockpit, reusing the search/gate floating-pane + `panopt:*` pipe pattern.
  Pick -> `switch_session`.
- **(C) Optional 6th sidebar rail** - probably NOT worth it (costs column space
  in every cockpit and is the one pane with no `ws`). A+B cover the need.

# Example scenarios
1. **Morning startup**: `panopt` -> board shows panopt (2 agents, 4
   in-progress), infra (agent ⚠ waiting), frontend (idle); jump to infra first
   because of the flag, then `Alt-0` to panopt.
2. **Mid-flight triage**: deep in panopt, an infra agent goes idle at a prompt;
   board's infra line flips to ⚠ waiting; `Alt-0`, `switch_session` to infra,
   answer, switch back - panopt agents never paused.
3. **New project**: open board -> "add project" -> type a repo path -> PANopt
   bootstraps that cockpit and switches in. No separate terminal.
4. **Manager roll-up** (ties to #118): teammate attaches read-only
   (`zellij watch` / read-only web token) to `panopt-home` for a live,
   input-less overview of every project's agent activity - a true panopticon.
5. **End-of-day cleanup**: board shows frontend ○ stopped; select -> resurrect
   or delete; daemon project row + history stay, only the session goes.
6. **Reconnect after reboot**: daemon up, projects table intact, no sessions;
   board shows all ◌ never started with persisted todo counts; pick one, it
   cold-starts. State was never tied to a live session.

# New surfaces required
- **MCP `project_list`** (#120) - thin read over projects +
  active_counts_by_project() + todo aggregates; daemon already has every field.
  Possibly `project_forget` for stale rows.
- **CLI `panopt switch` / `panopt home`** - renders the board (ratatui, same
  shape as search.rs/close_gate.rs), reconciles vs `list-sessions`, execs
  attach or bootstraps.
- **Plugin glue** - floating summon reuses the pipe pattern; in-session jumps
  use `switch_session`; cold-start handoff (#121) is the only piece without a
  template.

Design exploration spun out of the #117 / note #118 Zellij research. Question:
how should PANopt handle **multiple projects**? Today we punt and defer to
multiple `panopt` invocations. Follow-up todos: #120 (project_list MCP tool),
#121 (cold-start handoff spike). Related: [[#118]].

# Ground truth: what a "project" actually is today
- **Daemon: already multi-project.** `panopt-core` keys everything on
  `project: i64` - roster, locks, todos, notes all project-isolated
  (registry.rs, locks.rs). One DB, one daemon on 127.0.0.1:7600. The
  `projects` table stores `root TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` - i.e. **the daemon
  persists every project's absolute path**. MCP connections pick their project
  via `?ws=<abs-path>`. A second `panopt up` in another repo **reuses** the
  running daemon (`daemon::ensure` no-ops if the port is open).
- **Cockpit: single-project.** `session_name(project)` =
  `panopt-<basename>-<pathhash>`, and the layout bakes one `PROJECT` into every
  sidebar pane's `ws`/`cwd`. One Zellij session = one project's cockpit.

So "multiple instances" today is really **one shared daemon + N independent
cockpit sessions**, not multiple backends.

# The crux
The UI unit of "a project" is the **sidebar** (the five plugin panes, each
pinned to one `ws`). "Multiple projects in one cockpit" therefore means
**multiple sidebars**, and Zellij's only native container for that is **tabs**.
(Panes don't help: dropping project B's pane into project A's cockpit leaves
the sidebar still showing A.)

# Tabs vs. instances (compare & contrast)
| axis | multiple instances (today) | multiple tabs (tab/project) |
|---|---|---|
| new code | none | substantial |
| switch | detach/attach or OS window | Zellij tab key, in-viewport |
| single pane of glass | no | yes (tab bar = project list) |
| isolation | hard (separate sessions) | soft (shared session) |
| sidebar instances | 5 per open session | 5 x #tabs in one session |
| per-project multiplayer | natural (mirroring is per-session, #116) | broken (see below) |
| lifecycle | quit/resurrect one freely | one session; quit risks all |

Three things the **tab model fights** today:
1. `ws` is baked per-pane; `new_tab_template` is static and can't vary `ws` per
   tab, so native new-tab can't know which project a tab is for - PANopt would
   have to own tab creation.
2. Pipe narrowing is `mode`-only, not `ws`+`mode`; a broadcast `panopt:*` pipe
   would hit every project-tab's todos gatekeeper. The whole gate layer would
   need ws-awareness.
3. `mirror_session true` (#116) shares the active tab across clients, so two
   teammates can't sit on different project-tabs. (Unreleased Zellij changelog
   hints at per-client tab focus - "allow tabs to have different sizes if
   clients aren't focused on the same one" - but not shipped.)

Conclusion: don't cram projects into one session via tabs. **Stay
multi-session for isolation and add a project switcher.** Tabs become a clean
follow-on only once Zellij ships per-client tab focus AND the gate layer is
ws-aware.

# The switcher: why it's cheap
It's a **join of three things PANopt already has**, on a key it computes
deterministically:

    projects.root --session_name()--> expected Zellij session
                  --`zellij list-sessions`--> running? stopped? absent?
        + active_counts_by_project() + todo aggregates --> live badges

- `projects.root` gives the path; `session_name(root)` gives the session name
  (same fn the launcher uses).
- `active_counts_by_project()` already exists and is used in state.rs:216.
- up.rs:417 already shells `zellij list-sessions` and parses it
  (`session_state`, `strip_ansi`).
So the board is largely a *view*; the only net-new runtime mechanic is
cold-start handoff (#121).

# What each project row shows
    ● panopt    2 agents · 4 in-progress · 11 open    ~/cp/panopt
    ○ frontend  idle                                  ~/work/frontend  [stopped]
    ◌ infra     1 agent ⚠ waiting                      ~/ops/infra      [never started]
- glyph: ● live cockpit · ○ stopped/resurrectable · ◌ daemon state, no session.
- badges (all from data the daemon already holds): active agents, in-progress +
  open todos, locks held, last activity.
- `⚠ waiting` (agent idle at a prompt) makes the board a triage board, not just
  a launcher - this is where the #118 scrollback / `zellij subscribe`
  capability pays off.

# Three switching mechanics (target state decides the gesture)
1. **Live cockpit** -> plugin `switch_session(name)` (instant; source cockpit
   keeps running). From outside: `zellij attach <name>`.
2. **Stopped/resurrectable** -> `zellij attach` resurrects, or offer delete
   (up.rs already handles the dead-session case).

   session, attach). This cold-start handoff is the one genuinely new mechanic

  `panopt-home` session whose sole content is the board. Morning entry point /
  fallback. One session, one pane, no per-project sidebar.

  in every cockpit and is the one pane with no `ws`). A+B cover the need.

Excellent! Now I have all the information. Let me create a comprehensive summary report:

## Project-Identity Data Layer Analysis

Based on my thorough exploration of the panopt-core codebase, here are the key findings:

### 1. **Projects Table Schema and Path Resolution**

**File: `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/db.rs:22-28`**

The `projects` table schema:
```sql
CREATE TABLE projects (
    id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    root               TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    next_todo_id       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    next_scratchpad_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
);
```

- **`root TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`** (line 25): Canonicalized filesystem path, enforces one project per path
- **Project identity**: `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` — opaque auto-incremented project id
- **Before V5**: Three per-type counters (`next_todo_id`, `next_scratchpad_id`, `next_roster_id`)
- **V5 onward** (line 16, const SCHEMA_VERSION = 9): Unified `next_id` counter across all resource types

**Path Resolution Functions:**

- **`Store::ensure_project(root: &Path)`** (state.rs:89-117): 
  - Canonicalizes the path to collapse symlinks and trailing slashes
  - Queries: `SELECT id FROM projects WHERE root = ?1` (line 94-100)
  - Creates project row on first sight: `INSERT INTO projects (root) VALUES (?1)` (line 105-106)
  - Returns `ProjectId(i64)` wrapper for all subsequent queries

**Key insight**: Project identity is decoupled from projection path. The `root` column is the sole lookup key; the canonical path ensures stability even if called with different symlink or slash variants.

---

### 2. **Forward-Only Migration Mechanism**

**File: `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/db.rs:14-302`**

**Version Tracking:**
- **SCHEMA_VERSION constant** (line 16): `const SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = 9;` — current schema version
- **Storage mechanism**: `PRAGMA user_version` — SQLite's built-in schema versioning (line 270)

**Migration Pattern:**
```rust
pub(crate) fn migrate(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
    let version: i64 = conn.pragma_query_value(None, "user_version", |r| r.get(0))?;
    if version < 1 { conn.execute_batch(SCHEMA_V1)?; }
    if version < 2 { conn.execute_batch(SCHEMA_V2)?; }
    // ... V3-V8 follow the same pattern
    if version < 9 { apply_v9(conn)?; }
    if version != SCHEMA_VERSION {
        conn.pragma_update(None, "user_version", SCHEMA_VERSION)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

**V1-V6 Schema Blocks:**
- **V1** (line 22): Initial 3-table schema (projects, todos, scratchpads)
- **V2** (line 53): Todo full data model + side tables (comments, blockers)
- **V3** (line 97): Roster table (agents/commands/terminals)
- **V4** (line 129-147): Timestamps on scratchpads — **uses `apply_v4(conn)` function** for idempotency guard
- **V5** (line 163-172): Unify counters into `next_id` — **uses `apply_v5(conn)` function**
- **V6** (line 194-236): Split roster → `agent_tools` + `processes` — **uses `apply_v6(conn)` function**
- **V7** (line 311-317): Soft delete (nullable `deleted_at`) — **uses `apply_v7(conn)` function**
- **V8** (line 327-329): Tags on scratchpads — **uses `apply_v8(conn)` function**
- **V9** (line 346-351): Rename `scratchpads` → `notes` — **uses `apply_v9(conn)` function** with guard against drift

**Idempotency Guards:**
- Complex migrations (V4, V8, V9) use **`table_exists(conn, table)`** (lines 356-363) or **`add_column_if_missing()`** (lines 245-262) to tolerate dev-database drift where columns/tables were added before `user_version` bump landed

**To Add New Migration V10:**
1. Add `const SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = 10;` (increment line 16)
2. Create a new `fn apply_v10(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> { ... }` function
3. Add block in `migrate()`: `if version < 10 { apply_v10(conn)?; }`
4. Define migration SQL/logic inside `apply_v10()`

---

### 3. **Filesystem Projection: Atomic Write + Rename Pattern**

**File: `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/projection.rs:1-108`**

**Atomic Write Mechanism:**

```rust
fn atomic_write(target: &Path, contents: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    let parent = target.parent().ok_or(...)?;
    let file_name = target.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()).ok_or(...)?;

    let seq = TMP_SEQ.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let tmp = parent.join(format!(".{file_name}.tmp.{}.{seq}", std::process::id()));

    match fs::write(&tmp, contents).and_then(|()| fs::rename(&tmp, target)) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(e) => {
            let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp);
            Err(e)
        }
    }
}
```

**Key Pattern:**
- **Temp file naming** (line 98): `.{filename}.tmp.{pid}.{seq}` — process id + per-process atomic counter prevent collisions under concurrent writes
- **Atomic rename** (line 100): `fs::rename(&tmp, target)` — atomic on same filesystem (guaranteed by creating temp in same parent dir)
- **Cleanup on error** (lines 102-107): Remove temp file if rename fails

**Projection Location vs. Identity:**
- **Root path** is stored in `projects.root` (the identity)
- **Projection directory**: `<root>/.panopt/` (state.rs:1454-1464: `project_root()` resolves identity to path, then calls projection functions)
- **Per-file locations** (projection.rs:24-79):
  - Todos: `.panopt/todos.md` (index), `.panopt/todos/{id}.md` (per-item)
  - Notes: `.panopt/notes.md` (index), `.panopt/note/{id}.md` (per-item)
  - Agents: `.panopt/agents.md`
  - Locks: `.panopt/locks.md`
  - Agent tools: `.panopt/agent_tools.md`
  - Processes: `.panopt/processes.md`

**Projection Flow** (state.rs:1467-1558):
Each mutation calls `reproject_*()`, which:
1. Retrieves project root via `project_root(project)` query (line 1454-1464)
2. Calls projection module function with full path
3. Projection module uses `atomic_write()` for all `.md` file updates

---

### 4. **Aggregate Functions: `active_counts_by_project()` and Project Listing**

**File: `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/registry.rs:192-211`**

```rust
pub(crate) fn active_counts_by_project(&self, within: Duration) -> Vec<(i64, usize)> {
    let now = SystemTime::now();
    let mut counts: Vec<(i64, usize)> = self
        .by_project
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|(pid, m)| {
            let n = m
                .values()
                .filter(|a| {
                    now.duration_since(a.last_seen)
                        .map(|idle| idle <= within)
                        .unwrap_or(true)
                })
                .count();
            (n > 0).then_some((*pid, n))
        })
        .collect();
    counts.sort_by_key(|(pid, _)| *pid);
    counts
}
```

**Called from** (state.rs:214-220):
```rust
pub fn connected_agents_by_project(&self) -> Vec<(ProjectId, usize)> {
    self.registry
        .active_counts_by_project(ACTIVE_PRESENCE)
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(pid, n)| (ProjectId(pid), n))
        .collect()
}
```

**Related Functions:**
- **`active_total(within)`** (registry.rs:176-187): Total agent count across all projects within time window
- **`connected_agent_count()`** (state.rs:206-208): Simple wrapper around `registry.active_total(ACTIVE_PRESENCE)`

**Key Details:**
- Returns `Vec<(project_id: i64, agent_count: usize)>` filtered to projects with **at least one live agent**
- "Live" = touched within `ACTIVE_PRESENCE` duration (state.rs:47: `const ACTIVE_PRESENCE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5)`)
- Sorted by project id for stable output
- Used by SIGTERM handler to decide whether shutdown would drop a client (state.rs:194-208 comment)

**Other Project Listing/Aggregate Functions:**
- **`project_root(project)`** (state.rs:1454-1465): Query to resolve `ProjectId` → filesystem path
- No global "list all projects" function exists — the daemon is per-project (each project has its own `.panopt/` tree and writes to a shared SQLite db; queries are parameterized by `project_id`)

---

## Summary Table

| Component | Location | Key Elements |
|-----------|----------|--------------|
| **Schema** | db.rs:22-28 | `root TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, `next_id` (V5+) |
| **Path→ID Lookup** | state.rs:89-117 | `ensure_project()` canonicalizes, queries/creates row |
| **Migration Version** | db.rs:16 | `SCHEMA_VERSION = 9`, `PRAGMA user_version` |
| **Migration Blocks** | db.rs:18-351 | V1-V9 defined; `apply_Vx()` functions for complex steps |
| **Idempotency Guards** | db.rs:245-363 | `add_column_if_missing()`, `table_exists()` |
| **Atomic Writes** | projection.rs:85-108 | Temp file + rename pattern, `.tmp.{pid}.{seq}` |
| **Projection Paths** | projection.rs:24-79 | `.panopt/{todos,notes,agents,locks,agent_tools,processes}.md` |
| **Active Agents** | registry.rs:192-211 | `active_counts_by_project()` filters by `last_seen` within window |
| **SIGTERM Gate** | state.rs:193-208 | Uses `connected_agent_count()` to prevent dropping live clients |

```rust
    let version: i64 = conn.pragma_query_value(None, "user_version", |r| r.get(0))?;

    if version < 9 { apply_v9(conn)?; }
```

```rust
fn atomic_write(target: &Path, contents: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    let parent = target.parent().ok_or(...)?;
    let file_name = target.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()).ok_or(...)?;

    let seq = TMP_SEQ.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let tmp = parent.join(format!(".{file_name}.tmp.{}.{seq}", std::process::id()));

    match fs::write(&tmp, contents).and_then(|()| fs::rename(&tmp, target)) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(e) => {
            let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp);
            Err(e)
        }
    }
}
```

**Key Pattern:**
- **Temp file naming** (line 98): `.{filename}.tmp.{pid}.{seq}` — process id + per-process atomic counter prevent collisions under concurrent writes
- **Atomic rename** (line 100): `fs::rename(&tmp, target)` — atomic on same filesystem (guaranteed by creating temp in same parent dir)
- **Cleanup on error** (lines 102-107): Remove temp file if rename fails

```rust
pub(crate) fn active_counts_by_project(&self, within: Duration) -> Vec<(i64, usize)> {
    let now = SystemTime::now();
    let mut counts: Vec<(i64, usize)> = self
        .by_project
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|(pid, m)| {
            let n = m
                .values()
                .filter(|a| {
                    now.duration_since(a.last_seen)
                        .map(|idle| idle <= within)
                        .unwrap_or(true)
                })
                .count();
            (n > 0).then_some((*pid, n))
        })
        .collect();
    counts.sort_by_key(|(pid, _)| *pid);
    counts
}
```

# Plan: Decompose project-identity redesign (note #123 / todo #124) into todos

## Context

Note **#123** argues PANopt's project identity is currently a filesystem **path**
(`projects.root TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`), but a project is really a **repo** that can
be cloned to any path, moved, checked out as a worktree, or mirrored on another
machine — all of which fragment one logical project today. It establishes that
identity **cannot be derived** from git (a fork shares upstream's whole history →
identical root-commit hash → over-merges), so identity is human *intent*: a
committed `.panopt/project-id` UUID on top of a fallback resolver. The structural
move is to split the two roles `?ws=` conflates — **identity** (opaque repo key,
resolved at the edge) vs **projection** (`ws=<path>`, where `.panopt/*.md` is
written).

Todo **#124** already captures this as an umbrella with a "Work items" list, and it
**blocks #120** (project_list switcher board) which **blocks #121** (cold-start
spike). This task does not write code — it **breaks #124 into 5 executable child
todos** and wires them as blockers of #124, so the epic (and the switcher work
behind it) stays blocked until the pieces land.

This is a **todo-authoring task only** (no source edits). The file/line references
below are recorded in each todo body so the eventual implementer starts oriented.

## Confirmed code seams (recorded for the implementer)

- **Schema** — `crates/panopt-core/src/db.rs`: `projects` table at `db.rs:22-28`
  (`root TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, unified `next_id` since V5). Forward-only
  migrations via `PRAGMA user_version`; `SCHEMA_VERSION = 9` at `db.rs:16`; add a
  new `apply_v10()` + `if version < 10 { apply_v10(conn)?; }` step. Idempotency
  helpers `add_column_if_missing()` / `table_exists()` already exist.
- **Path→ProjectId** — `Store::ensure_project()` at `state.rs:89-117`
  (canonicalize → `SELECT id FROM projects WHERE root=?` → insert).
- **`?ws=` routing** — `panoptd/src/handler.rs:421-449`: `query_param()` extractor
  and `resolve_project()` (errors if `ws` missing). This is the seam to add a
  `project=` param.
- **Edge / launcher** — `crates/panopt/src/agent_config.rs:29-77` builds the
  `_mcp-proxy` args (`--ws`, `--id`, `--name`, `--token`); `resolve_ws()`,
  `default_id()` (`$USER-$HOSTNAME`). `crates/panopt/src/up.rs` `session_name()`
  (`panopt-<basename>-<pathhash>`, ~`up.rs:385`), `zellij list-sessions` (~`up.rs:417`);
  pane env injection (`PANOPT_AGENT/NAME/TOKEN/WS`) in `crates/panopt/src/agent.rs:75-81`.
- **CLI** — clap `Cmd` enum in `crates/panopt/src/main.rs:45-247`; new `Project`
  subcommand slots beside `Up` / `AgentConfig`.
- **No git helpers exist anywhere in the workspace** — the resolver is net-new and
  **must live in `panopt` (the edge), not `panopt-core`** (the core boundary forbids
  git/rmcp/tokio deps; verify with `cargo tree -p panopt-core`).
- **`.panopt/` writes** — atomic temp+rename in `panopt-core/src/projection.rs:85-108`;
  `.panopt/.gitignore` is written as `*` (`projection.rs:352-375`) — note the
  `project-id` file must be **committed**, so the resolver/init must not let it be
  ignored.

## The 5 child todos to create (tags: `multi-project`, `identity`; each blocks #124)

1. **Schema: add opaque `identity` key + forward-only migration + back-fill**
   - New `apply_v10()` in `db.rs`: bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` to 10, add an
     `identity TEXT UNIQUE` column to `projects` (kept distinct from `root` so
     `root` remains the projection path). Back-fill every existing row with a
     derived key (path-based today) so no row is null. Update `ensure_project()`
     (`state.rs:89`) and add an `ensure_project_by_identity()`-style lookup.
   - Decision to record in the todo: new column vs. repurpose `root` (recommend
     **new column** — root still names the projection location).

2. **Edge resolver: compute the repo identity key (git logic, in `panopt`)**
   - New module in `crates/panopt` (NOT core). Resolver order: (1)
     `.panopt/project-id` UUID committed in tree → authoritative; (2) normalized
     remote origin URL (strip scheme/credentials/`.git`, lowercase host); (3)
     root-commit hash (`git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD`); (4) canonical path
     (non-git). Pure, unit-testable; shells `git`. No core dependency.

3. **Wire `project=` through the MCP URL, handler, and launcher edge**
   - `handler.rs:421-449`: parse `project=` via `query_param()`; when present,
     resolve identity → ProjectId; keep `ws=<path>` for projection; default
     `project` from the resolver (todo #2) when omitted (back-compat: `ws`-only
     still works).
   - `agent_config.rs` + `_mcp-proxy`: add `--project`/`project=` to the emitted
     args/URL. `up.rs`/`agent.rs`: inject the resolved identity (e.g.
     `PANOPT_PROJECT`) into panes alongside `PANOPT_WS`.
   - Depends on #1 (column to store) and #2 (resolver to compute).

4. **`panopt project init` subcommand**
   - New `Project { init }` variant in `main.rs` clap enum. Writes/rewrites
     `.panopt/project-id` with a fresh UUID (how a fork declares itself separate,
     and how anything opts into a stable id). Ensure the file is **committed**, not
     caught by the `.panopt/.gitignore` (`*`). Uses the resolver's file format
     from #2.

5. **Docs: update DESIGN.md §5.3 (and note the switcher-row implication)**
   - Rewrite the worktree/path-identity paragraph (§5.3) to the
     identity-vs-projection split; cross-reference #123/#124 and note that the
     #120 switcher board keys rows on repo identity with checkouts listed beneath.

## Wiring

- Create todos 1–5 (`todo_create`), each with `tags: ["multi-project","identity"]`
  and a body carrying the relevant seam references above plus a back-link to
  `note #123` / `#124`.

Net-new module that computes a project's stable identity key at the edge. Rationale
in note #123; umbrella is #124 (this blocks it).

Identity is human *intent*, not derivable data — a fork shares upstream's whole
history so the root-commit hash is identical and over-merges. So the resolver is a
fallback chain under a committed declaration.

## Resolver order (first match wins)
1. `.panopt/project-id` (UUID) committed in the tree -> **authoritative**.
2. else normalized remote origin URL — strip scheme/credentials/trailing `.git`,
   lowercase host.
3. else root-commit hash — `git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD`.
4. else canonical path (not a git repo) — today's behavior.

## Where / constraints
- Lives in `crates/panopt` (the edge), **NOT** panopt-core — the core boundary
  forbids a git dependency. There are currently NO git helpers anywhere in the
  workspace, so this shells `git` fresh.
- Pure and unit-testable: feed it a dir, assert the chosen key + which rule fired.
- Output is the opaque string that becomes `project=` on the MCP URL and the
  `identity` column value (#125).

Natural order: parallel with #125; #127 and #128 both consume this.

content.content:
1	//! SQLite schema and forward migrations for the persistent store.
2	//!
3	//! One database file holds every project. `todos` and `notes` are keyed
4	//! by `(project_id, id)`, so ids restart at 1 per project and the projected
5	//! files read naturally. The schema version is tracked in SQLite's
6	//! `user_version` pragma so later changes can migrate forward in place.
7	//!
8	//! Note: the `notes` table was called `scratchpads` through V8; the V1-V8
9	//! migration steps below keep that historical name and V9 renames it. Only
10	//! runtime code (and the schema as of V9) speaks of `notes`.
11	
12	use rusqlite::Connection;
13	
14	/// The current schema version. Bump this and add a step to [`migrate`]
15	/// whenever the schema changes.
16	const SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = 9;
17	
18	/// Version 1: the initial three-table schema.
19	///
20	/// Per-project id counters live on the `projects` row rather than being
21	/// derived from `MAX(id)`, so a deleted highest todo never causes id reuse.
22	const SCHEMA_V1: &str = "
23	CREATE TABLE projects (
24	    id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
25	    root               TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
26	    next_todo_id       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
27	    next_scratchpad_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
28	);
29	CREATE TABLE todos (
30	    project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id),
31	    id         INTEGER NOT NULL,
32	    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,
33	    status     TEXT    NOT NULL,
34	    PRIMARY KEY (project_id, id)
35	);
36	CREATE TABLE scratchpads (
37	    project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id),
38	    id         INTEGER NOT NULL,
39	    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,
40	    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,
41	    PRIMARY KEY (project_id, id)
42	);
43	";
44	
45	/// Version 2: the full todo data model (DESIGN.md Section 6.1).
46	///
47	/// Adds the descriptive columns to `todos` and the two side tables that hold a
48	/// todo's comments and its blocked-by relationships, both modeled on Solo's
49	/// schema. The `todo_blockers` table carries a foreign key on each of its two
50	/// todo references, so deleting a todo cascades away the rows where it is the
51	/// blocked todo *and* the rows where it is the blocker. Pre-existing `'done'`
52	/// todos (the only completed value the v1 schema knew) become `'completed'`.
53	const SCHEMA_V2: &str = "
54	ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN body            TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '';
55	ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN priority        TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium';
56	ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN assignee        TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '';
57	ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN tags            TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]';
58	ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN created_at      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '';
59	ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN updated_at      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '';
60	ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN completed_at    TEXT;
61	ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN next_comment_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;
62	UPDATE todos SET status = 'completed' WHERE status = 'done';
63	UPDATE todos
64	   SET created_at = datetime('now'), updated_at = datetime('now')
65	 WHERE created_at = '';
66	CREATE TABLE todo_comments (
67	    project_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
68	    todo_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
69	    id         INTEGER NOT NULL,
70	    author     TEXT    NOT NULL,
71	    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,
72	    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL,
73	    PRIMARY KEY (project_id, todo_id, id),
74	    FOREIGN KEY (project_id, todo_id)
75	        REFERENCES todos(project_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE
76	);
77	CREATE TABLE todo_blockers (
78	    project_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
79	    todo_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
80	    blocker_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
81	    PRIMARY KEY (project_id, todo_id, blocker_id),
82	    CHECK (todo_id != blocker_id),
83	    FOREIGN KEY (project_id, todo_id)
84	        REFERENCES todos(project_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
85	    FOREIGN KEY (project_id, blocker_id)
86	        REFERENCES todos(project_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE
87	);
88	";
89	
90	/// Version 3: the persistent agent/command/terminal roster (todo #67).
91	///
92	/// Adds one `roster` table holding all three kinds, distinguished by a `kind`
93	/// column, modeled on Solo's `processes` table. Like `todos` and `scratchpads`
94	/// it is keyed `(project_id, id)` with a per-project id counter on `projects`.
95	/// Columns are deliberately minimal; per-entry settings (auto-start, env, an
96	/// agent-tool link) are left for later additions.
97	const SCHEMA_V3: &str = "
98	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN next_roster_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;
99	CREATE TABLE roster (
100	    project_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id),
101	    id           INTEGER NOT NULL,
102	    kind         TEXT    NOT NULL,
103	    name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
104	    display_name TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
105	    command      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
106	    cwd          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
107	    position     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
108	    created_at   TEXT    NOT NULL,
109	    PRIMARY KEY (project_id, id)
110	);
111	";
112	
113	/// Version 4: timestamps on scratchpads (todo #76).
114	///
115	/// Adds `created_at` and `updated_at` to `scratchpads` so every mutation -
116	/// including append - can bump `updated_at` and the projected index line can
117	/// surface it. That makes the cockpit sidebar visibly refresh on every
118	/// scratchpad change, the same way every todo mutation already changes the
119	/// todo index line through its status/priority fields. The backfill mirrors
120	/// the v1->v2 todo backfill: any pre-existing scratchpad lands with both
121	/// timestamps set to `datetime('now')`.
122	///
123	/// The `ALTER`s run through [`add_column_if_missing`] rather than a raw
124	/// `execute_batch`, so a database stuck at `user_version = 3` whose
125	/// `scratchpads` table already carries the v4 columns - the transitional
126	/// state of any machine that ran an in-development v4 binary before the
127	/// `user_version` bump landed - upgrades cleanly instead of failing on
128	/// "duplicate column name". The backfill is unconditionally safe.
129	fn apply_v4(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
130	    add_column_if_missing(
131	        conn,
132	        "scratchpads",
133	        "created_at",
134	        "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''",
135	    )?;
136	    add_column_if_missing(
137	        conn,
138	        "scratchpads",
139	        "updated_at",
140	        "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''",
141	    )?;
142	    conn.execute_batch(
143	        "UPDATE scratchpads
144	            SET created_at = datetime('now'), updated_at = datetime('now')
145	          WHERE created_at = '';",
146	    )
147	}
148	
149	/// Version 5: unify per-resource id counters into one global `next_id` (todo #16).
150	///
151	/// Before V5 every project row carried three independent counters -
152	/// `next_todo_id`, `next_scratchpad_id`, `next_roster_id` - so the same number
153	/// could be handed out as a todo *and* a scratchpad *and* a roster entry. V5
154	/// replaces them with a single `next_id` so a `#N` reference points to exactly
155	/// one resource type forever. Existing rows are left in place: SQLite's
156	/// `(project_id, id)` primary keys are per-table, so any collision in the
157	/// pre-V5 data persists as-is and only the fresh allocations after the
158	/// migration are guaranteed unique.
159	///
160	/// The seed for `next_id` is `max(old three counters)`, which is the lowest
161	/// value safe against every pre-existing id in any of the three tables. The
162	/// three old columns are then dropped.
163	fn apply_v5(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
164	    conn.execute_batch(
165	        "ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN next_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;
166	         UPDATE projects
167	            SET next_id = MAX(next_todo_id, next_scratchpad_id, next_roster_id);
168	         ALTER TABLE projects DROP COLUMN next_todo_id;
169	         ALTER TABLE projects DROP COLUMN next_scratchpad_id;
170	         ALTER TABLE projects DROP COLUMN next_roster_id;",
171	    )
172	}
173	
174	/// Version 6: split the hybrid `roster` table into a config layer
175	/// (`agent_tools`) and an instance layer (`processes`) (todo #27).
176	///
177	/// A V5 roster row was both a config (name, command, cwd) and the implicit
178	/// single instance of that config; liveness was derived from Zellij pane state,
179	/// never stored. V6 mirrors Solo's two-layer model: `agent_tools` holds the
180	/// durable configurations, `processes` holds per-project instances and carries
181	/// a nullable FK back to its source tool plus nullable lifecycle columns
182	/// (`pid`, `status`, `agent_state`, `last_seen`) so a follow-up that owns
183	/// process spawn can populate them without another migration.
184	///
185	/// Both new tables keep drawing ids from the unified `projects.next_id`
186	/// counter introduced by V5, so a `#N` reference still resolves to exactly one
187	/// row across todos, scratchpads, agent_tools, and processes.
188	///
189	/// Migration of existing rows: `kind='agent'` becomes an `agent_tools` row
190	/// (configuration), and `kind='command'` / `kind='terminal'` become
191	/// `processes` rows (instances - the only thing the pre-split roster ever was
192	/// for those kinds). Ids are preserved verbatim since both new tables share
193	/// the same `next_id` sequence the originals were drawn from.
194	fn apply_v6(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
195	    conn.execute_batch(
196	        "CREATE TABLE agent_tools (
197	             project_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id),
198	             id           INTEGER NOT NULL,
199	             name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
200	             display_name TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
201	             command      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',

238	/// Add `column` to `table` only if it is not already there. Used by migrations
239	/// that may collide with a transitional dev-database state where the column
240	/// landed before its `user_version` bump did. `decl` is the type+constraint
241	/// text after the column name, exactly as it would appear in an `ALTER TABLE`.
242	///
243	/// `column` and `table` are fixed in-crate identifiers, not caller input, so
244	/// interpolating them into the SQL is safe.
245	fn add_column_if_missing(
246	    conn: &Connection,
247	    table: &str,
248	    column: &str,
249	    decl: &str,
250	) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
251	    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(&format!("PRAGMA table_info({table})"))?;
252	    let mut rows = stmt.query([])?;
253	    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
254	        let existing: String = row.get(1)?;
255	        if existing == column {
256	            return Ok(());
257	        }
258	    }
259	    drop(rows);
260	    drop(stmt);
261	    conn.execute_batch(&format!("ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {decl};"))
262	}

264	/// Bring `conn` up to [`SCHEMA_VERSION`], creating tables on a fresh database.
265	///
266	/// Idempotent: a database already at the current version is left untouched.
267	/// Each step is gated on the stored `user_version`, so a v1 database upgrades
268	/// in place and a fresh one runs every step in order to the same end state.
269	pub(crate) fn migrate(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
270	    let version: i64 = conn.pragma_query_value(None, "user_version", |r| r.get(0))?;
271	    if version < 1 {
272	        conn.execute_batch(SCHEMA_V1)?;
273	    }
274	    if version < 2 {
275	        conn.execute_batch(SCHEMA_V2)?;
276	    }
277	    if version < 3 {
278	        conn.execute_batch(SCHEMA_V3)?;
279	    }
280	    if version < 4 {
281	        apply_v4(conn)?;
282	    }
283	    if version < 5 {
284	        apply_v5(conn)?;
285	    }
286	    if version < 6 {
287	        apply_v6(conn)?;
288	    }
289	    if version < 7 {
290	        apply_v7(conn)?;
291	    }
292	    if version < 8 {
293	        apply_v8(conn)?;
294	    }
295	    if version < 9 {
296	        apply_v9(conn)?;
297	    }
298	    if version != SCHEMA_VERSION {
299	        conn.pragma_update(None, "user_version", SCHEMA_VERSION)?;
300	    }
301	    Ok(())
302	}

304	/// Version 7: soft delete (todo #54).
305	///
306	/// Each item-bearing table grows a nullable `deleted_at` column. `*_delete`
307	/// stamps it with `datetime('now')` instead of issuing a `DELETE FROM`, and
308	/// every read path (`*_list`, `*_get`, `fetch_*`, the blocker-resolution helper)
309	/// filters on `deleted_at IS NULL`. The row stays behind so a future undelete
310	/// surface has something to revive; recovery / cleanup tooling is deferred.
311	fn apply_v7(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
312	    add_column_if_missing(conn, "todos", "deleted_at", "TEXT")?;
313	    add_column_if_missing(conn, "scratchpads", "deleted_at", "TEXT")?;
314	    add_column_if_missing(conn, "agent_tools", "deleted_at", "TEXT")?;
315	    add_column_if_missing(conn, "processes", "deleted_at", "TEXT")?;
316	    Ok(())
317	}

319	/// Version 8: tags on scratchpads (todo #61).
320	///
321	/// Scratchpads grow the same `tags` column todos got in V2, stored as a JSON
322	/// array string with default `'[]'`. The vocabulary is shared with todos -
323	/// `state::tags_list` returns the union across both kinds - so a tag chosen on
324	/// one surface is offered up on the other. The column uses
325	/// [`add_column_if_missing`] for the same dev-database drift case the earlier
326	/// scratchpad migration (V4) guarded against.
327	fn apply_v8(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
328	    add_column_if_missing(conn, "scratchpads", "tags", "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'")
329	}

331	/// Version 9: rename the `scratchpads` table to `notes` (todo #79).
332	///
333	/// "Scratchpad" implied an ephemerality the concept never had - these are
334	/// durable, append-oriented, shared documents that agents and humans both read
335	/// and write. The rename is the whole change: the columns, the unified
336	/// `projects.next_id` counter, and the tag vocabulary shared with todos are all
337	/// untouched, and every pre-existing scratchpad survives as a note with its id
338	/// and body intact. Whether notes should additionally carry a `type`
339	/// (note/plan/memory/inter-agent) is deferred to a follow-up.
340	///
341	/// Guarded like the column migrations against dev-database drift: an
342	/// in-development V9 binary may have renamed the table before its
343	/// `user_version` bump landed, so a database reporting V8 might already have a
344	/// `notes` table. Skip the rename in that case instead of failing on
345	/// "no such table: scratchpads".
346	fn apply_v9(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), rusqlite::Error> {
347	    if table_exists(conn, "notes")? {
348	        return Ok(());
349	    }
350	    conn.execute_batch("ALTER TABLE scratchpads RENAME TO notes;")
351	}

353	/// True if a table named `table` exists. Used by migrations that must stay
354	/// idempotent against a transitional dev-database that already applied a
355	/// rename or create before its `user_version` bump landed.
356	fn table_exists(conn: &Connection, table: &str) -> Result<bool, rusqlite::Error> {
357	    let count: i64 = conn.query_row(
358	        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = ?1",
359	        [table],
360	        |r| r.get(0),
361	    )?;
362	    Ok(count > 0)
363	}

+/// Version 10: project identity distinct from the projection path (note #123,
+/// Through V9 a project *was* its filesystem path: `projects.root` was both the
+/// identity key (the unique row) and the projection location (where `.panopt/*.md`
+/// is written). That conflation fragments one logical project the moment its repo
+/// is cloned to another path, moved, checked out as a worktree, or mirrored on
+/// another machine. V10 splits the two roles: `root` stays the projection
+/// location, and a new `identity` column holds an opaque, stable repo key.
+/// Identity is computed at the edge (the launcher / agent-config), never derived
+/// inside core - so to `panopt-core` it is just an opaque string, and no git
+/// dependency crosses the core boundary. The key cannot be a `UNIQUE` column on
+/// an `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` (SQLite forbids it), so the column is added plain,
+/// back-filled from `root` to preserve today's one-project-per-path behavior for
+/// every existing row, then a unique index enforces distinctness going forward.
+/// Guarded like the other column migrations against dev-database drift: the
+/// `ADD COLUMN` runs through [`add_column_if_missing`] and the index is
+/// `IF NOT EXISTS`, so a database that ran an in-development V10 binary before its
+/// `user_version` bump landed upgrades cleanly. The back-fill only touches rows
+/// whose `identity` is still NULL, so it is safe to re-run.

417	/// Find `key`'s value in a URL query string, percent-decoded.
418	///
419	/// `query` is the raw query component, with no leading `?`, as returned by
420	/// [`http::Uri::query`].
421	fn query_param(query: Option<&str>, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
422	    let prefix = format!("{key}=");
423	    let raw = query?
424	        .split('&')
425	        .find_map(|kv| kv.strip_prefix(prefix.as_str()))?;
426	    Some(
427	        percent_encoding::percent_decode_str(raw)
428	            .decode_utf8_lossy()
429	            .into_owned(),
430	    )
431	}
432	
433	/// Resolve the project for a request from the `ws` query parameter on the MCP
434	/// server URL.
435	///
436	/// Agents register PANopt per project with `?ws=<project path>` appended to the
437	/// URL, so the daemon scopes every call without inferring anything. The path is
438	/// percent-decoded, so workspace paths containing spaces survive the round trip.
439	fn resolve_project(store: &mut Store, parts: &Parts) -> Result<ProjectId, McpError> {
440	    let path = query_param(parts.uri.query(), "ws").ok_or_else(|| {
441	        McpError::invalid_params(
442	            "no project: the MCP server URL must end with ?ws=<absolute project path>",
443	            None,
444	        )
445	    })?;
446	    store
447	        .ensure_project(std::path::Path::new(&path))
448	        .map_err(map_core_err)
449	}
450	
451	/// The calling agent's stable key and the source it came from.
452	///
453	/// Prefers the `agent` query parameter on the MCP URL - a stable per-agent id
454	/// the launcher injects, which survives MCP session churn. Falls back to the
455	/// `mcp-session-id` header when no `agent` is set; that header rotates whenever
456	/// the client's connection drops and re-initializes, so without an `agent` id
457	/// one agent can briefly appear under several keys (see DESIGN.md Section 9).
458	/// `None` only for a request that carries neither.
459	///
460	/// The returned [`KeySource`] tells the registry how to age the entry:
461	/// declared identities never idle-prune, session ids do.
462	fn agent_key(parts: &Parts) -> Option<(String, KeySource)> {
463	    if let Some(id) = query_param(parts.uri.query(), "agent").filter(|id| !id.is_empty()) {
464	        return Some((id, KeySource::Declared));
465	    }
466	    parts
467	        .headers
468	        .get("mcp-session-id")
469	        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
470	        .map(|s| (s.to_string(), KeySource::Session))
471	}
472	
473	/// Resolve the request's project and register the calling agent in it.
474	///
475	/// Every tool runs this first, so any connected agent appears in the registry
476	/// even if it never calls `identify`. Returns the project and the agent key
477	/// (the latter `None` only when the request carries no MCP session id).
478	///
479	/// A request carrying `?observer=1` is a tool, not an agent - the `panopt`
480	/// CLI, say - so it resolves the project but is never added to the registry,
481	/// and its key is reported as `None`.
482	///
483	/// On first-sight of a stable `?agent=` key, a `?name=<friendly>` parameter
484	/// on the URL is applied as an implicit `agent_identify`. This lets a
485	/// hand-launched agent declare its display name once in the MCP URL instead
486	/// of needing to call `identify` on every reconnect.
487	fn enter(store: &mut Store, parts: &Parts) -> Result<(ProjectId, Option<String>), McpError> {
488	    let project = resolve_project(store, parts)?;
489	    if query_param(parts.uri.query(), "observer").as_deref() == Some("1") {
490	        return Ok((project, None));
491	    }
492	    let Some((key, source)) = agent_key(parts) else {
493	        return Ok((project, None));
494	    };

String: /// Build the daemon URL with the project, agent id, and name as query params.
///
/// `ws` and `id` and `name` are percent-encoded so paths with spaces and
/// arbitrary display names survive. The daemon reads `ws` to scope the
/// project, `agent` to key the registry, and `name` for the display label.
fn build_url(base: &str, ws: &str, id: &str, name: &str) -> String {
    let enc = |s: &str| {
        percent_encoding::utf8_percent_encode(s, percent_encoding::NON_ALPHANUMERIC).to_string()
    };
    format!(
        "{base}?ws={ws}&agent={id}&name={name}",
        ws = enc(ws),
        id = enc(id),
        name = enc(name),

245	### 5.3 Transport
246	
247	The daemon listens on **HTTP/SSE (Streamable HTTP)**, not stdio.
248	
249	Rationale: stdio MCP is one-client-per-process. If agents used stdio, each
250	would spawn its own private copy of the daemon with no shared state, which
251	defeats the entire purpose. A shared coordination hub requires one daemon
252	serving many connections, which means a network transport. HTTP is chosen
253	because agent CLIs configure HTTP MCP servers by URL with no friction.
254	
255	The bind address is configurable (`panoptd --host <addr>`). It defaults to
256	`127.0.0.1` for single-machine use; setting `0.0.0.0` (or a specific
257	interface) lets agents on other hosts join the coordination plane - an agent
258	on a Mac driving Solo, an agent on a host with USB-attached debug hardware,
259	etc. Every request, loopback or remote, must carry a bearer token via
260	`Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or `?token=<token>` as a fallback for
261	clients that cannot set headers). The token is generated by the daemon on
262	first boot at `<data-dir>/panopt/token` with mode 0600 and shared with local
263	clients via the filesystem; remote agents copy it over a secure channel.
264	Always-required auth is a uniform gate rather than a per-host policy: the
265	token file is owner-readable, so a process able to read it is already in the
266	same trust domain as the daemon, and a single rule is simpler to reason
267	about than "loopback unauthenticated, remote authenticated." The user-facing

### 5.3 Transport

The daemon listens on **HTTP/SSE (Streamable HTTP)**, not stdio.

Rationale: stdio MCP is one-client-per-process. If agents used stdio, each
would spawn its own private copy of the daemon with no shared state, which
defeats the entire purpose. A shared coordination hub requires one daemon
serving many connections, which means a network transport. HTTP is chosen
because agent CLIs configure HTTP MCP servers by URL with no friction.

The bind address is configurable (`panoptd --host <addr>`). It defaults to
`127.0.0.1` for single-machine use; setting `0.0.0.0` (or a specific
interface) lets agents on other hosts join the coordination plane - an agent
on a Mac driving Solo, an agent on a host with USB-attached debug hardware,
etc. Every request, loopback or remote, must carry a bearer token via
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or `?token=<token>` as a fallback for
clients that cannot set headers). The token is generated by the daemon on
first boot at `<data-dir>/panopt/token` with mode 0600 and shared with local
clients via the filesystem; remote agents copy it over a secure channel.
Always-required auth is a uniform gate rather than a per-host policy: the
token file is owner-readable, so a process able to read it is already in the
same trust domain as the daemon, and a single rule is simpler to reason
about than "loopback unauthenticated, remote authenticated." The user-facing
recipe for the cross-machine case - `panopt up --host 0.0.0.0` on the
daemon host, `panopt token` to extract the token, and `panopt agent-config
--host <addr> --token <value>` on the agent host - lives in the README.

There is one daemon instance, and it serves every project at once. A project
is selected per connection by a `ws` query parameter on the MCP URL:
`http://HOST:PORT/mcp?ws=<absolute project path>&agent=<id>&name=<friendly>&token=<token>`.
An agent's launcher (cockpit-spawned or `panopt agent-config` for
hand-launched) captures that path from `$PWD`, so registration is the moment
the project is named - the daemon never has to guess. The daemon
canonicalizes the path, so symlinks and trailing slashes collapse onto one
project, and distinct git worktrees are distinct projects unless deliberately
pointed at the same path. The URL also carries an `agent` parameter (a
stable per-agent id used as the registry key) and an optional `name`
parameter that the daemon applies as an implicit `identify` on first sight,
so a single URL is enough to land an agent as a first-class citizen
(Sections 6.3 and 9). Every project's state lives in one SQLite database the
daemon owns (Section 6.4).

### 5.4 Coordination plane (agents to daemon)

This plane does not involve the host at all.

input.new_string:
There is one daemon instance, and it serves every project at once. A project
is selected per connection by two query parameters on the MCP URL, which
deliberately split two roles an earlier design conflated (note #123, todo
#124):
`http://HOST:PORT/mcp?ws=<absolute project path>&project=<identity>&agent=<id>&name=<friendly>&token=<token>`.

- **`ws` is the projection location** - the checkout whose `.panopt/*.md`
  mirror this connection reads and writes. It is inherently path-bound and is
  always required. The daemon canonicalizes it, so symlinks and trailing
  slashes collapse.
- **`project` is the identity** - an opaque, stable repo key the daemon uses
  as the database key, so the project a connection joins is decoupled from
  where it happens to be checked out. Two checkouts of one repo - at different
  paths, in separate worktrees, or on different machines - share one project
  row when they resolve to the same identity. When `project` is omitted the
  daemon falls back to keying on the canonical `ws` path (the original
  behavior), so a path-only client still works.

Identity is resolved **at the edge** - the proxy/`agent-config`, never the
daemon - so no git dependency crosses into `panopt-core`; to the daemon the key
is an opaque string. The resolver is a fallback chain, first match wins:

1. a `.panopt/project-id` (a UUID) committed in the tree - authoritative;
2. else the normalized remote origin URL;
3. else the root-commit hash;
4. else the canonical `ws` path (a non-git directory).

Identity is **not** derived purely from git, because git cannot answer the
real question. A fork shares its upstream's entire history, so they have an
identical root-commit hash - deriving identity from it would silently merge a
fork into its upstream. "Same project?" is human intent, not data, so the
committed `project-id` sits on top of the chain: `panopt project init` writes
(or rewrites) it, which is how a fork declares itself separate and how any tree
opts into an id that travels with it. The file is the one thing under
`.panopt/` that is committed rather than ignored (the projection `.gitignore`
is `*\n!project-id\n`).

The cross-project switcher (todo #120) builds on this: a project row keys on
repo identity and lists its *checkouts* (the paths/sessions) beneath it, rather
than presenting each checkout as its own project.

The URL also carries an `agent` parameter (a stable per-agent id used as the
registry key) and an optional `name` parameter that the daemon applies as an
implicit `identify` on first sight, so a single URL is enough to land an agent
as a first-class citizen (Sections 6.3 and 9). Every project's state lives in
one SQLite database the daemon owns (Section 6.4).

Once the new code is running, the resolver normalizes your origin to:


Every clone/worktree/machine of this repo resolves to that same key, so they all coordinate as one project. **Nothing to do** — this is the default for any repo with a remote.

### B. Declared — identity = a committed UUID
Only needed if you want identity to survive a remote-URL change, or to split a fork from upstream:

```bash
panopt project init        # writes .panopt/project-id with a fresh UUID
```

```diff
+    atomic_write(&panopt_dir(ws).join(".gitignore"), "*\n!project-id\n")?;
```

The mechanism: `.panopt/.gitignore` is `*` (ignore the whole projection) plus `!project-id` (re-include just that one file). The negation works because `.panopt/` itself isn't excluded by a parent rule, so git can re-include a file inside it.

**The design is Claude-free.** `.panopt/project-id`, the resolver, and `panopt project init` are pure git/filesystem. Nothing about *identity* needs Claude.

**My #127 wiring was incomplete** — that's the real issue. I only taught the **MCP proxy** (the thing `claude --mcp-config` spawns) to send `project=` to the daemon. But every other client connects with `ws=` only:

- `panopt todo` / `note` / `process` / `agent-tool` / `id-kind` all go through one helper, `observer_url(ws, port)` in `todo.rs:115` — and it appends only `&ws=…&observer=1`.

So today the daemon only *learns* the identity when something connects through the Claude-spawned proxy. That's not the design — it's just the one edge I happened to wire.

**The correct fix:** resolve identity at *every* client edge, not just the proxy. The CLI already funnels through `observer_url()`, so adding `&project={resolve(ws).key}` there (plus the 2–3 other builders) makes the daemon key on identity for **any** client. Concretely, after that fix you could re-key this repo's row by running `panopt todo ls` in a shell — no Claude anywhere in the loop.

That also means the daemon never resolves git itself (it can't — for a remote agent the `ws` path lives on the agent's host, so identity must be computed client-side, where the working tree actually is). Edge resolution is right; I just need it at *all* edges.

## What changed

**Fix 1 — identity works without Claude (#131).** The gap was that only the MCP proxy (the Claude-spawned client) sent `project=`. I moved identity resolution to the shared CLI choke point:
- `todo.rs::observer_url()` now appends `&project=…` — and since *every* CLI subcommand, `search`, the cockpit viewer panes, and the edit/forms route through it, they're all covered in one edit.
- `agent.rs::leave()` (its own URL) also sends it.

Identity stays **edge-resolved**, not daemon-resolved — correct, because for a remote agent the `ws` path only exists on the agent's host, so only the client can resolve it.

**Proof:** `panopt id-kind 124` — a plain shell command, zero Claude — re-keyed this repo's row from the path to the committed UUID. You can verify identity any time with `sqlite3 ~/.local/share/panopt/panopt.db "SELECT root, identity FROM projects"`.

**Fix 2 — `project init` repairs the `.gitignore` (#132).** It now runs `git check-ignore -v` after writing the id; if a `.panopt/` *directory* exclusion is why the id is ignored, it rewrites that one line to `.panopt/*` + `!.panopt/project-id`. Other cases get a clear `git add -f` note instead of a silent failure. I also already fixed this repo's root `.gitignore` by hand, so your commit will work now.

**Verification:** 159 panopt + 103 core tests pass (incl. 2 new gitignore tests + a real-git end-to-end), clippy clean, diff confined to the intended files.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Project identity: repo-based key, split from projection path

Key a PANopt project on a stable repo identity instead of its checkout
path, so a repo cloned to another path, moved, in a worktree, or mirrored
on another machine coordinates as one project (note #123, todo #124).

- Split the two roles `?ws=` conflated: `ws` stays the projection
  location, a new opaque `project=` identity becomes the DB key.
- panopt-core: V10 migration adds a back-filled `identity` column +
  unique index; `ensure_project_by_identity` looks up by identity and
  adopts/re-keys a legacy path row in place (path callers never clobber
  an established identity).
- Edge resolver (panopt crate, not core - no git dep crosses the
  boundary): committed `.panopt/project-id` -> remote URL -> root commit
  -> path. Forks can't be git-derived (shared history), so a committed
  UUID sits on top.
- Identity resolved at every client edge: the MCP proxy and the shared
  CLI `observer_url` both send `project=`, so it works with or without
  Claude. Daemon falls back to path identity when `project=` is absent.
- `panopt project init` writes/rewrites the committed UUID and repairs an
  ancestor `.gitignore` that excludes `.panopt/` (a dir exclusion blocks
  re-including the id; rewrite to `.panopt/*` + `!.panopt/project-id`).
- DESIGN.md 5.3 rewritten for identity-vs-projection.

Tests: V10 migration + adoption, resolver chain, URL wiring, project
init + gitignore repair. Full workspace test + clippy clean.
EOF
